channel.title: Acme: W3C Changes
channel.description: Reports on substantive changes in W3C GitHub repositories.

item.title: SPARQL Update Examples Adopt RDF 1.2 Triple-Term Reification
item.description:
The SPARQL 1.2 Update draft has rewritten its INSERT and DELETE examples around RDF 1.2 triple terms. The examples now use rdf:reifies and show the equivalent reifying-triple and annotation syntaxes.

The revision makes explicit that recording a claim about a triple term does not assert that triple. Applications must insert or delete the asserted triple separately when that is the intended operation.

Changes: sparql-update commit af1ef8a7.

item.title: SHACL 1.2 Lets Rule Sets Act as Validation Entailments
item.description:
The SHACL 1.2 Inference Rules draft now allows a named rule set to be used as an sh:entailment value. A validation engine can therefore execute only the selected rules before validation instead of always running every rule in the shapes graph.

The draft distinguishes shape rules from global rules, states that neither runs automatically during ordinary validation, and requires an engine to fail when it cannot support a requested entailment regime.

Changes: data-shapes commit 2ada6ac4.

item.title: SHACL 1.2 Adds a Non-Validating Code-Type Hint
item.description:
SHACL 1.2 Core now defines sh:codeType, an annotation that tells API and code generators which datatype to expose for a shape’s values. It is independent of validation constraints such as sh:datatype, sh:class, and sh:nodeKind.

A shape can consequently validate an IRI while asking generated code to present it as a string. The hint is language-neutral and does not change validation results.

Changes: data-shapes commit af518a38.

item.title: SHACL 1.2 Can Mark Data Nodes as Incomplete
item.description:
SHACL 1.2 Core now defines sh:incomplete and sh:incompleteURIStart for declaring that a node intentionally has only partial data. The declaration does not alter conformance or the validation report.

Tools may use the annotation to present likely incompleteness-related violations differently—for example, downgrading a missing required value while data entry is unfinished. An explicit false value overrides an incomplete declaration.

Changes: data-shapes commit f39b1d48.

item.title: YAML Vocabulary Generator Adds Fine-Grained JSON-LD Context Controls
item.description:
W3C’s YAML-to-vocabulary generator now supports property-scoped contexts, clearing an inherited context, language maps, and top-level terms selected by vocabulary scope. A vocabulary range can also generate @type: @vocab in JSON-LD without affecting the RDFS output.

The release adds an html_class option as well. Together, the features let one YAML vocabulary definition produce more precise JSON-LD contexts and formatted documentation.

Changes: yml2vocab commit db3566a9.

item.title: CSS Sizing Draft Adds a Functional stretch() Value
item.description:
CSS Sizing Level 4 now defines stretch(length-percentage), which sizes a box so its margin box fits the supplied size. The fit-content() formula is correspondingly expressed in terms of stretch().

The draft also specifies fallback behavior when fit-content() creates a cyclic percentage dependency: maximum, minimum, and preferred sizing properties fall back to max-content, min-content, and fit-content respectively. This remains developing Level 4 behavior.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 50337328; csswg-drafts commit 77c73372; csswg-drafts commit 062dc948.

item.title: RDF 1.2 Aligns Parser Behavior for Non-Conforming Documents
item.description:
The RDF 1.2 drafts for N-Quads, N-Triples, Turtle, TriG, and RDF/XML now consistently leave the result of parsing non-conforming input undefined. Error detection, reporting, and recovery are implementation choices because appropriate behavior depends on the surrounding API or protocol.

N-Quads also gains a future-proofing rule: any later incompatible syntax that reuses the media type must carry a VERSION value newer than 1.2, allowing older parsers to recognize unsupported input.

Changes: rdf-n-quads commit af9193d2; rdf-n-quads commit 6873719a; rdf-xml commit e7111c9a; rdf-n-triples commit 96167c3f; rdf-turtle commit 94c6e4a5; rdf-trig commit b3579511.

item.title: RDF and SPARQL Tests Expand Version, Scope, and Language-Tag Coverage
item.description:
The W3C RDF test suite now checks the N-Triples 1.2 VERSION declaration, including wrong case, non-string values, and Turtle-style variants. SPARQL tests add post-query VALUES scope after GROUP BY and VALUES behavior inside GRAPH with FROM NAMED.

Another case confirms that STRLANG language tags compare without regard to case. The additions target parsing, dataset scoping, and literal equality edge cases that have produced implementation disagreement.

Changes: rdf-tests commit 42e6bb1d; rdf-tests commit ec2ba15e; rdf-tests commit 8dd12bf6; rdf-tests commit 9382f411.

item.title: CSS Defines a Separate Parser for Style Attributes
item.description:
CSS Syntax now defines dedicated algorithms for parsing and consuming a style attribute. Unlike a block’s contents, a style attribute has no wrapping block, does not let a closing brace terminate parsing, ignores at-rules, and treats qualified rules as syntax errors.

The explicit entry point gives HTML style attributes and CSSStyleDeclaration.cssText a common parsing model without conflating them with full nested rule blocks.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 64e5504c.

item.title: IFT Encoder Improves Multi-Script Font Segmentation
item.description:
The Incremental Font Transfer encoder’s experimental auto-segmentation pipeline now supports multiple frequency profiles, groups overlapping writing scripts, and can choose a merge depth automatically. Its heuristic merger can batch compatible segments while enforcing a 20 KB patch-size ceiling.

Follow-up fixes cover probability caching, segment reassignment, scripts with no overlap, and an unsigned-underflow bug in Brotli binary-diff allocation. This is implementation work in the developing encoder, not a change to the IFT specification.

Changes: ift-encoder commit 59678059; ift-encoder commit 2443c996; ift-encoder commit 74d6a4c6; ift-encoder commit fa521403; ift-encoder commit 7d695cc4.

item.title: CSS Animation Triggers Define Event Functions and a Range Shorthand
item.description:
The CSS Animation Triggers draft now enumerates event functions such as click(), pointerdown(), focusin(), input(), and change(), plus keypress() with an optional key value. It also defines timeline-trigger-range as a shorthand for activation and active ranges.

The main timeline-trigger shorthand now incorporates that range shorthand. This is early draft work and the supported event-function set may still change.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 72248154; csswg-drafts commit 1e921957; csswg-drafts commit b4b69f6c.

item.title: CSS Color Publishes Sample EdgeSeeker Gamut-Mapping Pseudocode
item.description:
CSS Color 4 now includes sample pseudocode for the EdgeSeeker gamut-mapping algorithm, including construction of its reusable lookup table and mapping of individual colors. Follow-up fixes improve numerical stability, close lookup curves correctly, and avoid remapping colors already in gamut.

The sample is restricted to RGB destination spaces with non-imaginary primaries, excluding spaces such as ProPhoto RGB. The detailed algorithm gives implementers a common reference for wide-gamut color conversion.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 9a923136; csswg-drafts commit 6fa56e0b; csswg-drafts commit 778ad60b; csswg-drafts commit 58408a4a; csswg-drafts commit 5e7e5034; csswg-drafts commit 536e7ec9.

item.title: ActivityPub Clarifies Optional Delivery to Additional Shared Inboxes
item.description:
ActivityPub now says a server MAY deliver a public activity to additional shared inboxes beyond those required by the normal recipient and forwarding rules. The previous wording referred ambiguously to “all known” shared inboxes.

The clarification preserves the optional behavior while avoiding an implication that a server should broadcast to every shared inbox it has ever discovered.

Changes: activitypub commit bcbabdef.

item.title: SPARQL Query Refines Logical-Not and Property-Path Definitions
item.description:
The SPARQL 1.2 query draft now declares sparql:logical-not as a FunctionalForm, matching its special evaluation behavior rather than treating it as an ordinary function.

The draft also removes redundant formulas beneath predicate property-path evaluation, leaving the normative algebra definition as the source of behavior. The cleanup reduces conflicting formal descriptions.

Changes: sparql-query commit e4682c6b; sparql-query commit f0527967.

item.title: HTML Diff Tool Repairs Relative Links in Comparison Output
item.description:
W3C’s HTML comparison tool now resolves relative links against each source document before producing a diff. Links and images no longer become relative to the diff viewer itself, where they could point to the wrong location or break.

The change applies base-URL handling while the source HTML is parsed, preserving meaningful navigation in generated specification comparisons.

Changes: htmldiff-ui commit 562f2a81.

item.title: CSS Counter Styles Clarifies UA-Drawn Marker Fallbacks
item.description:
CSS Counter Styles now allows browsers to draw the predefined symbolic markers with an image or chosen font wherever those styles are used, not only through list-style-type. When a generated glyph cannot be used inside a counter() value, the browser may fall back to the style’s string definition.

The draft also makes directional disclosure markers explicitly respond to both writing mode and text direction.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit d8fdab81.

item.title: CSS Experiments with a New Computed Model for Automatic Quotes
item.description:
The CSS Generated Content draft has reworked how the quotes property carries an automatically selected language through inheritance. A provisional placeholder keyword replaces match-parent while the working group settles the final name and computed-value model.

The intended behavior is clearer than the temporary spelling: when the inherited value is auto, the child retains the parent’s content language so quotation marks remain consistent. This is unresolved draft work, not author-ready syntax.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit c8459c50.

item.title: CSS Marks Counters in Generated Alt Text as At Risk
item.description:
CSS Generated Content Level 3 now marks the use of counters inside content alternative text as an at-risk feature. The designation means the feature may be removed before advancement if implementation experience is insufficient.

The specification describes itself as a rough draft not ready for implementation, so the status is a warning about stability rather than a removal from deployed CSS.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 0a439193.

item.title: CSS Grid Renames flow-tolerance to fit-tolerance
item.description:
The CSS Grid Level 3 draft has renamed the grid-lanes placement control flow-tolerance to fit-tolerance. The property sets the size difference below which tracks are treated as equivalent, reducing visually arbitrary backtracking during auto-placement.

This is a name change in developing grid-lanes syntax; implementations and examples following the draft should use fit-tolerance.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 0ff603b4.

item.title: CSS Form-Control Pseudo-Elements Standardize on border-box
item.description:
The CSS Forms draft now places box-sizing: border-box in the user-agent stylesheet for all defined form-control pseudo-elements, including checkmarks, picker icons, slider parts, field components, step controls, and placeholders.

Applying one sizing model across these generated parts makes their declared dimensions include borders and padding and reduces reliance on browser-specific defaults.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 0289e95a.

item.title: Media Capture Extensions Exposes Supporting Interfaces in Workers
item.description:
The Media Capture Extensions draft now exposes OverconstrainedError to dedicated workers because MediaStreamTrack.applyConstraints() can reject with that type there. It likewise exposes MediaStreamTrackEvent because worker-exposed MediaStream objects fire those events.

The temporary partial-interface declarations keep worker behavior usable until the exposure sets can be merged into the base Media Capture specification.

Changes: mediacapture-extensions commit ba7d096c.

item.title: WoT Adds a Draft EtherNet/IP Binding
item.description:
The Web of Things Binding Templates repository now includes a draft EtherNet/IP binding. It defines eip: URI forms, primitive and structured tag types, byte and bit offsets, polling and timeout controls, scaling, and operations for reading, writing, and observing properties.

A JSON Schema and examples accompany the vocabulary. This is draft protocol-binding work intended for industrial devices, not a finalized W3C Recommendation.

Changes: wot-binding-templates commit 92538eb2.

item.title: SHACL-SPARQL Rules Tighten Blank-Node and Error Semantics
item.description:
The SHACL SPARQL Rules draft now defines blank nodes in rule-body triple patterns as variables, including blank nodes nested in triple terms. Repeated occurrences map to the same fresh variable.

Expression evaluation now propagates errors explicitly and filters out error results before effective-boolean-value testing. A rewritten well-formedness section tracks which variables are in scope after each rule element, preparing the model for aggregates.

Changes: data-shapes commit 25aaa15a; data-shapes commit 658045bb; data-shapes commit f5fdd1f0.

item.title: CSS Line Clamping Keeps Hidden Content Accessible
item.description:
CSS Overflow now defines clamped content as visually suppressed rather than removed from the box tree. It is not painted and does not enlarge scrollable overflow, but it remains in sequential focus navigation and the accessibility tree.

The draft also renames continue: auto to continue: normal, changes line-clamp’s longhand expansion, and specifies that block-ellipsis processing occurs before text-overflow ellipsing.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 1dafa605; csswg-drafts commit 1f04ca5c; csswg-drafts commit bf9279ef.

item.title: Pointer Scrolling Promises Report Whether a Scroll Was Interrupted
item.description:
CSSOM View now resolves scroll(), scrollTo(), and scrollBy() promises with a ScrollResult dictionary containing an interrupted flag. Starting another scroll on the same container resolves pending operations as interrupted; a completed operation returns false.

Viewport scrolling combines the layout and visual viewport results, reporting success only when both finish without interruption. Scripts can now distinguish completion from supersession instead of receiving an undefined value in either case.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 2b26877d.

item.title: WebCodecs Corrects Video-Frame Layout and Pixel-Format Rules
item.description:
WebCodecs now throws TypeError when a VideoFrame’s computed display width or height is zero. It also fixes allocation calculations for odd-width subsampled images, interleaved components such as NV12, and packed RGB formats.

Separate corrections identify the proper opaque equivalents for I422AP10, I422AP12, and I444AP12. Together, the changes prevent undersized buffers and inconsistent interpretation of high-bit-depth alpha formats.

Changes: webcodecs commit 7be36992; webcodecs commit 6f4d6eb8; webcodecs commit 924a4f84; webcodecs commit 6d8e3d36; webcodecs commit 3d4b1131.

item.title: CSS Extends Opacity Serialization Beyond the opacity Property
item.description:
CSS Color 4 now states that opacity-value serialization rules apply to every property that accepts that type, not only the opacity property. The draft cites shape-image-threshold as an example.

The clarification makes percentage and number serialization consistent wherever the shared grammar is used.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 4dd6b0d7.

item.title: Browser Testing Charter Draft Expands into Agentic Browsing
item.description:
The draft Browser Testing and Tools Working Group charter now describes browser automation as useful to end users as well as test developers. Its proposed scope explicitly includes agentic browsing, where a user employs tools to drive a browser through complex tasks.

The draft also adds coordination with the Web Machine Learning Community Group, where WebMCP is incubated. This broadening is a charter proposal, not yet an approved expansion of the group’s mandate.

Changes: charter-drafts commit bc1e0898.

item.title: Draft Sustainable Web Charter Defines Guidelines and Impact Ratings
item.description:
A new draft charter proposes a Sustainable Web Interest Group whose mission is to improve digital sustainability for people and the planet. Its scope covers web design and development, authoring tools, user agents, hosting, infrastructure, product strategy, and measurable impact data.

Proposed deliverables include maintaining the Web Sustainability Guidelines and their Impact Ratings, improving conformance targets and metrics, and producing educational material. Native-application concerns outside the Web and most hardware manufacturing are out of scope. This is an early draft, not an approved charter.

Changes: charter-drafts commit 7f4d6552.

item.title: Ask I18N Improves Code Blocks, Definitions, and Source Citations
item.description:
Ask I18N’s Markdown renderer now accepts language names such as C++, C#, and objective.c, supports longer fenced blocks, escapes unclosed code, and avoids a parser hang on malformed fence information.

The retrieval system also indexes the internationalization navigation pages and recognizes definition questions such as “What is i18n?” Citations to those pages now use their correct public URLs.

Changes: ask-i18n commit 8a14b597; ask-i18n commit 8bee4d0d.

item.title: Trusted Types Adds Policy-Controlled Sanitizer Options
item.description:
The Trusted Types draft introduces TrustedHTMLParserOptions and a policy createParserOptions hook for HTML-parsing sinks. A policy can provide a reviewed Sanitizer configuration and control script execution while allowing a raw string to be parsed without first creating TrustedHTML.

The algorithms reject unsafe combinations in which author-supplied sanitizer settings have not been vetted. String-only sinks and XML documents still require TrustedHTML through createHTML.

Changes: trusted-types commit fbe9462f.

item.title: WCAG ACT Rule Removes searchbox from Name-from-Content Roles
item.description:
The ACT rule for checking that a visible label appears in an accessible name no longer lists searchbox among roles that derive their name from content. The role does not support that naming behavior under the rule’s applicability model.

The correction prevents evaluators from applying the Label in Name test to search boxes on an invalid premise.

Changes: wcag-act-rules commit 48edc0a3.

item.title: Message Resources Draft Allows Blank Lines Inside Messages
item.description:
The developing Message Resources syntax now permits empty lines inside a multi-line message value. Continuation lines may be indented or blank, and leading and trailing empty lines are trimmed from the resolved value.

The grammar also clarifies escaping around frontmatter-like identifiers and line whitespace. This is proposal work in the internationalization discussion repository, not a published Recommendation.

Changes: i18n-discuss commit 7699b9ea.

item.title: SVG List Accessors Must Preserve Object Identity
item.description:
The SVG specification now says repeated getItem() calls for the same list index return the same object until the list changes. This applies to SVG list interfaces such as transform and length lists.

The identity guarantee prevents wrappers from appearing to change between reads and aligns the prose and examples with existing expectations for mutable SVG list items.

Changes: svgwg commit 47e645ef.

item.title: WebTransport Response Headers Are No Longer SameObject
item.description:
The WebTransport draft has removed the Web IDL SameObject annotation from responseHeaders. Repeated access is no longer required to return the identical Headers wrapper.

The header contents remain available, but implementations gain flexibility to create a fresh object rather than maintaining JavaScript object identity for the lifetime of the connection.

Changes: webtransport commit 7d19557f.

item.title: VC Render Method Renames Delivery Properties
item.description:
The Verifiable Credential Render Method draft now calls the transport hint deliveryMode rather than deliveryMethod. In the same model, the static render suite replaces the earlier nfc suite name and uses a delivery mode such as nfc when a template is intended for that channel.

The rename separates the rendering suite from the way rendered output is delivered. This is draft vocabulary and may still evolve.

Changes: vc-render-method commit a22ebe02; vc-render-method commit 44163d4b.

item.title: LWS Charter Draft Sets Delivery Dates and Adds Social-Web Coordination
item.description:
The draft Linked Web Storage Working Group charter now proposes Q1 2028 completion for the core protocol and its OpenID, SAML, and controlled-identifier authentication suites. Its timeline also names 2027 Candidate Recommendation targets and later dates for index services and the threat model.

The charter adds coordination with the Social Web Working Group to explore LWS use in social platforms and ActivityPub-related integration. These remain proposed dates and relationships in a draft charter.

Changes: lws-wg-charter commit be11e010; lws-wg-charter commit 4b998e66.

item.title: Reffy Cleans Up Indirect CSS Values Across Specification Levels
item.description:
Reffy now follows syntax references across all crawled CSS specifications to distinguish genuinely dangling values from values that apply indirectly through another property or type. Those false warnings are removed during post-processing.

Its series handling also becomes conservative when a crawl has missing specification levels: extracts on both sides of a gap are retained because the tool cannot safely identify the newest applicable level.

Changes: reffy commit 810f7e70; reffy commit bdb7ad01.

item.title: VC API Threat Model Adds QR Shoulder-Surfing Risk
item.description:
The draft VC API Lifecycle and Management threat model now covers attackers photographing an interaction QR code and using its URL on another device. The accompanying guidance favors holder-initiated cross-device flows, which reduce the chance that a visible code grants control to an observer.

The API draft also warns implementers to consider interaction-URL exposure in cross-device designs. This is evolving threat-model guidance, not a claim that QR flows are universally unsafe.

Changes: vcalm commit 274ed6b6; vcalm commit 5e4e15c0; vcalm commit 2e2e41bd.

item.title: SHACL 1.2 Tests Declare Which Processor Features They Require
item.description:
The SHACL 1.2 test suite now defines conformance identifiers for Core, Inference Rules, Node Expressions, SPARQL validation, custom functions, and SPARQL-RL syntax and evaluation. Tests use mf:requires to identify the processor capabilities they exercise.

This lets implementations run the relevant subset and report support without implying conformance to SHACL features they do not implement.

Changes: data-shapes commit 162b8580.

item.title: Push API Separates Declarative Notifications from Service Workers
item.description:
The Push API now explicitly fetches resources for a declarative push notification without involving a service worker when no environment settings object exists. The notification show steps receive null in that case.

This keeps icons and other notification resources loadable for declarative delivery while preserving the design goal that no service worker must run.

Changes: push-api commit 9adf83e7.

item.title: Linked Web Storage Switches Its Required Patch Format
item.description:
The Linked Web Storage Protocol draft now requires servers to support and advertise JSON Patch for partial updates to resources and linkset metadata. JSON Merge Patch remains an optional alternative.

The baseline Accept-Patch value changes to application/json-patch+json, aligning required behavior with RFC 6902 and giving clients operation-based edits rather than whole-member replacement semantics.

Changes: lws-protocol commit ef02548b.

item.title: Push API Formalizes Subscription Encryption Keys
item.description:
The Push API now defines each subscription’s P-256 ECDH key pair and authentication secret as explicit associated data. Creation and getKey() algorithms spell out how the public key and authentication secret are generated and returned.

PushSubscriptionJSON also replaces an open-ended keys record with a dictionary containing p256dh and auth. The tighter model aligns the Web API with RFC 8291 encryption material.

Changes: push-api commit 0f5bfe6c.

item.title: WCAG Guidance Broadens Its View of Accidental Character-Key Shortcuts
item.description:
The Understanding document for WCAG 2.1.4 now explains accidental character-key shortcut activation as a concern for keyboard and screen-reader users as well as people using speech input. It retains the core advice that authors let users turn off, remap, or limit single-character shortcuts to the component that has focus.

The revision adds a key-event logger to help people discover which printable-key shortcuts a page exposes. This is informative WCAG guidance, not a change to the success criterion itself.

Changes: wcag commit 31c9b262.

item.title: SPARQL 1.2 Tightens the Formal Rules for Ordering and Expression Evaluation
item.description:
The SPARQL 1.2 query draft now uses a single ordering-condition model for ORDER BY, replacing overlapping comparator terminology and making the algebra easier to follow. It also explicitly defines evaluation of a variable as its RDF term when bound and as an error when unbound.

A related clarification enumerates the possible variable-or-term combinations in NPS evaluation. Together, the edits reduce ambiguity for implementers of sorting and path evaluation in the developing SPARQL 1.2 specification.

Changes: sparql-query commit b55ebb36; sparql-query commit 7f707ffe; sparql-query commit be19f51e.

item.title: W3C CSS Validator Adds Nesting and @scope Support
item.description:
The W3C CSS Validator can now parse nested rules, resolve nested selectors, and validate scoped style blocks. Its @scope handling also recognizes @keyframes and @font-face within a scope under the CSS Cascading Level 6 rules.

A follow-up fixes detection of custom properties nested inside calc(), avoiding false validation results when variables appear below the top level of a value. The changes make the validator useful for more modern CSS without treating these constructs as syntax errors.

Changes: css-validator commit 95ef4b6e; css-validator commit 8c452afe; css-validator commit f4cf8d53; css-validator commit 25ff4879.

item.title: RDF Test Suite Adds Edge Cases for GRAPH, VALUES, and Relative IRIs
item.description:
The W3C RDF test repository now covers several SPARQL graph-pattern edge cases: VALUES inside GRAPH when the graph variable is absent, nested GRAPH patterns, and LIMIT or OFFSET subqueries that must be evaluated separately for each named graph.

A further SPARQL 1.0 test checks relative-IRI resolution. These cases give query-engine implementers more precise interoperability checks around dataset scoping and base-IRI handling.

Changes: rdf-tests commit 5e5da96b; rdf-tests commit 8df7fc13; rdf-tests commit 047ddf97; rdf-tests commit ca72fa96.

item.title: MathML Full Drops Two Legacy Alignment Elements
item.description:
The MathML Full draft has removed malignmark and maligngroup, two legacy elements for decimal and marker-based alignment that were already absent from MathML Core. The document points authors who still need the behavior to a polyfill.

This narrows the larger MathML vocabulary around features with viable implementation paths. The edit affects the evolving MathML Full draft; it does not remove anything from MathML Core.

Changes: mathml commit 3ebba291.

item.title: ActivityPub Makes Public Outbox Responses a Normative Recommendation
item.description:
The ActivityPub specification now says a server SHOULD return all Public posts when an unauthenticated client requests an actor's outbox. The wording previously used a lowercase “should,” leaving its normative force unclear.

Capitalizing the RFC 2119 keyword makes the existing expectation explicit for server implementers while preserving it as a recommendation rather than an absolute requirement.

Changes: activitypub commit cca3043d.

item.title: EPUB 3.4 Marks the source-of Metadata Property as Outdated
item.description:
The EPUB 3.4 draft now lists the source-of metadata property among outdated features. Existing publications that use it remain conforming, but authors are no longer encouraged to rely on it for new content.

The change preserves compatibility while signalling where the format is moving. Reading systems still need to tolerate the property in older EPUB content.

Changes: epub-specs commit 358cb418.
